title: U-Fund: A New Page
tagline: A team project for requesting, approving and funding books for people in prison
summary: U-Fund: A New Page was my SWEN 261 team project. We built a full-stack app where incarcerated people could request books, prison staff could approve or deny them, and people outside could pay for the approved ones. It was one of my first times working on a big app with several kinds of users across a whole team.

hero.alt: A New Page inmate request screen showing two requested books and their costs
hero.caption: An inmate could submit book requests and keep track of the books attached to their account.

sections.heading: Working as a team
body: This was a really fun project because the four of us had to work on both sides of a big system together. I worked with Liam Pennino, Nina Sagawa and Selene Shen. We split features between the Angular front end and the Spring Boot back end, and then had to make sure everything fit together.
It was real practice at dividing up work, reading other people's code, and building features that depended on a teammate's part. We didn't use any AI on it.

sections.heading: Three kinds of users
body: Inmates request books. Admins review those requests and approve or deny them with a message. Helpers browse the approved books, add them to a basket and check out (the payment was simulated). Each step sends the inmate a notification, which was one of the features we added on top of the requirements.

sections.heading: How we built it
body: The back end is Java and Spring Boot, split into controllers, data access and models, and it saves everything to JSON files. The front end is Angular, with a page and a set of routes for each kind of user.

sections.heading: Testing
body: We tested with JUnit, in the browser, and with curl. By the final presentation every part of the back end had at least 91% test coverage. We also ran SonarQube and went through what it found, and we listed the issues we'd clean up next.

notes: UPDATED FROM USER INTERVIEW, SOURCE REVIEW, AND THE SWEN 261 GROUP 3C ARCHIVE SUPPLIED 2026-09-15. The archive contains requirements, domain and class diagrams, acceptance-test plans, sprint documents, a 21-slide final presentation dated 2025-04-23, and four demo recordings. The five UI images on this page were extracted from current_swen_261_sprint_3_demo.mp4, the latest recording by timestamp, at approximately 02:00, 09:00, 10:30, 13:00, and 13:30. The frames were cropped to remove browser chrome, the Windows taskbar, and the Vimeo webcam overlay; their application content was not recreated. Existing architecture and sequence diagrams are authentic files from docs/. The final presentation confirms the four-person team, inmate role and notification enhancements, JUnit plus manual and curl testing, at least 91 percent coverage in every tier, 100 percent model-tier branch coverage, and the SonarQube examples described on the page. Date 2025-04 comes from the archive index's last team commit and the final presentation date. The source was not run because dependencies were deliberately excluded from the temporary archive and the JSON data files are mutated at runtime. Authentication and payment are course-project simulations and should not be described as production security or real payment processing. No public repository URL was verified.
